title: 118. Dr. Sasha Heinz on Improving Your Life with Developmental + Positive Psychology Principles
description_html:
Today's guest is Sasha Heinz, PhD, MAPP—a developmental psychologist and life coach who is an expert in positive psychology, lasting behavioral change, and the science of getting unstuck. In her private coaching practice, she teaches clients the tools to change their lives for good. Heinz received her BA from Harvard, her PhD in development psychology from Columbia, and her master’s in applied positive psychology from the University of Pennsylvania, where she also served as a faculty member (go Quakers!!). We discuss how attending therapy can help you with 'adulting', how to use coping skills in daily life, the myths around toxic positivity, how to improve your life using positive psychology, and misconceptions about improving your well-being.

Dr. Heinz's Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/drsashaheinz/?hl=en

guests: dr. sasha heinz, developmental psychologist and life coach
summary: sadie talks with dr. sasha heinz, a developmental psychologist and coach, about how positive psychology and developmental principles can help you actually feel better—not just analyze what's broken. dr. heinz shares her own recovery from bulimia, explains why focusing on strengths (not just wounds) can be more healing, and breaks down brain biases like hedonic adaptation and the availability heuristic that keep you feeling stuck. listeners learn practical ways to build mental fitness, why comparing yourself to your past self (not your peers) matters, and how well-being is about meaning, connection, and engagement—not just happiness.
quote: mental health is a commitment to reality at all costs.
